design.text: Single, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, active-controlled Phase 3 trial comparing Defencath catheter lock solution to the active control heparin (1,000 USP units/mL)

citations.quote: The efficacy and safety of Defencath were evaluated in a single, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, active-controlled Phase 3 trial, LOCK-IT-100, in patients with kidney failure receiving HD through a CVC.
LOCK-IT-100 evaluated the efficacy and safety of Defencath as a catheter lock solution (CLS) compared to the active control, heparin (1,000 USP units/mL), in reducing the incidence of CRBSIs.

result.text: Final analysis: 9 CAC-adjudicated CRBSIs (Defencath) vs 32 (heparin), 71% risk reduction (95% CI 38%, 86%), p=0.0006; hazard ratio 0.29 (95% CI 0.14, 0.62)

citations.quote: The final analysis at the completion of the study showed 9 CRBSI cases in the Defencath arm and 32 CRBSI cases in the heparin arm. This result was statistically significant in favor of Defencath (71% risk reduction, 95 % confidence interval, 38%, 86%, p=0.0006).

indication.text: Indicated to reduce the incidence of catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSI) in adult patients with kidney failure receiving chronic hemodialysis (HD) through a central venous catheter (CVC); indicated for a limited and specific population

citations.quote: LIMITED POPULATION: DEFENCATH® is indicated to reduce the incidence of catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSI) in adult patients with kidney failure receiving chronic hemodialysis (HD) through a central venous catheter (CVC). This drug is indicated for use in a limited and specific population of patients [see *Clinical Studies* (14)].

target_moa.text: Combination of taurolidine, a thiadiazinane antimicrobial (a derivative of aminosulfonamide-taurinamide) that transfers methylol groups interacting with bacterial and fungal cell walls, and heparin, an anticoagulant; taurolidine reacts with cell wall constituents of gram-negative bacteria and neutralizes endotoxin activity

citations.quote: Defencath contains taurolidine (13.5 mg/mL), a thiadiazinane antimicrobial, and heparin (1,000 USP Units/mL), an anticoagulant, as the active ingredients, and citrate as a pH buffer.

modality.text: Small molecule (taurolidine) combined with heparin, formulated as a catheter lock solution

citations.quote: Defencath is a catheter lock solution (CLS) which contains taurolidine (13.5 mg/mL) and heparin (1,000 USP units/mL) as the active ingredients and citrate as a pH buffer. Taurolidine is a derivative of aminosulfonamide-taurinamide.

key_safety.text: Most frequent adverse reactions (≥2%): hemodialysis catheter malfunction (17% vs 12% heparin), hemorrhage/bleeding (7% vs 9%), nausea (7% vs 11%), vomiting (6% vs 8%), dizziness (6% vs 4%), and thrombocytopenia (2% vs 1%). Loss of catheter patency occurred more frequently in the Defencath arm (63 subjects, 16%) vs heparin (48 subjects, 12%). Serious adverse reactions in 40% (Defencath) vs 42% (heparin).
